rows.name: Salesforce Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved, by substantial majority, to assign Salesforce Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.893. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Salesforce's durable competitive moat — evidenced by thirteen consecutive years of global CRM market leadership, 77% gross margins, and a $72 billion contracted backlog — is now augmented by a credible AI monetization inflection via Agentforce, whose $1.5 billion ARR growing at 240% year-over-year offers a plausible path to revenue re-acceleration atop an already formidable platform. The most significant dissent, advanced by Mr. Greenblatt, argued that single-digit organic revenue growth and current valuation multiples do not offer sufficient margin of safety, warranting a PASS. This view did not prevail because the Committee judged that at approximately 17× forward cash flow, the market is not yet pricing in the regime-shift potential of agentic AI adoption across Salesforce's 150,000-customer installed base. The Committee recommends initiating a BUY position at current levels.

rows.name: Nike Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has voted to assign Nike Inc. (NKE) a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.864. The dominant argument, advanced by Messrs. Marks and Greenblatt and ultimately endorsed by a majority, holds that Nike's well-documented operational difficulties and deeply pessimistic sentiment—including a roughly 75% drawdown and forced index deletion—have driven the stock to a valuation (1.2× EV/Revenue, 12.6× EV/EBITDA, 4.6% dividend yield) that more than compensates for near-term risks, while the underlying consumer franchise remains fundamentally intact. The most significant dissent came from Mr. Buffett, who questioned whether the competitive moat has durably eroded and whether current earnings power justifies even a discounted entry. This concern did not prevail because the majority judged that the present valuation already prices in permanent impairment, offering an asymmetric return profile even under conservative recovery assumptions. Ms. Wood's objection on innovation grounds was noted but deemed outside the applicable framework. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing appropriate to a turnaround thesis.

rows.name: Walt Disney Co.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns a BUY rating to DIS with a conviction score of 0.833. The dominant argument carrying the majority is that Disney's unrivaled collection of branded intellectual property — Marvel, Star Wars, Pixar, ESPN, and twelve theme parks — constitutes a durable competitive moat, and that at a forward P/E of approximately 13.67x and EV/EBITDA near 11x, the market has not fully priced in the company's long-term owner earnings power, particularly as streaming margins inflect upward and AI-driven monetization opportunities emerge. The most significant dissent, advanced by Mr. Greenblatt, held that Disney's return on capital is merely average, that capital allocation complexity clouds the earnings picture, and that at $103 the stock does not meet the threshold of obvious mispricing his framework demands. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the valuation discount to intrinsic value sufficient and the qualitative moat durable enough to compensate for near-term capital intensity. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Amazon.com Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Furton Research Investment Committee assigns Amazon.com Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.7. The dominant argument carrying the majority holds that AWS — as the largest global cloud infrastructure provider operating at a $169 billion annualized run rate — sits at the critical nexus of the AI compute buildout, and that the market is likely underestimating its forward earnings power as AI-driven demand compounds. Members Aschenbrenner, Marks, and Wood each independently concluded that this structural tailwind, combined with Amazon's custom silicon investments, advertising toll-booth economics, and platform convergence potential, justifies the current valuation. The most significant dissent came from Buffett and Greenblatt, who argued that at a $2.74 trillion market capitalization, the price demands flawless execution across enormous capital commitments and leaves insufficient margin of safety. This concern did not prevail because the majority judged it rooted in backward-looking valuation frameworks inadequate for capturing the magnitude of the AI infrastructure cycle now underway. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: Alphabet Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee has resolved to assign Alphabet Inc. a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.7. The dominant argument, advanced by Aschenbrenner, Marks, and Wood and carrying the majority, holds that Alphabet's $514 billion Cloud backlog growing $50 billion sequentially, 82% Cloud revenue growth, and deepening AI-infrastructure positioning represent a structural transformation whose full earnings power is not yet reflected in the current price — particularly given a trailing P/E of approximately 17, which the majority views as restrained relative to the growth trajectory. The most significant dissent, articulated by Buffett and Greenblatt, centered on an EV/FCF multiple of roughly 75x and an implied earnings yield of approximately 1.3%, arguing that even extraordinary business quality cannot justify such a premium absent greater margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because the majority concluded that trailing free-cash-flow metrics understate forward owner earnings in a period of accelerating Cloud and AI monetization. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing appropriate to the valuation risk acknowledged in dissent.

rows.name: Microsoft Corp.
rows.statement: After full deliberation, the Committee assigns Microsoft a final score of **0.69** and recommends a **BUY**. The dominant argument, advanced by Aschenbrenner, Marks, and Wood and carrying the majority, holds that Microsoft's unmatched position as the primary large-cap vehicle for AI monetization — evidenced by a $37 billion AI annual run rate growing 123% year-over-year, Azure's 39% growth, and deep OpenAI integration — justifies current valuations given the extraordinary and still-expanding revenue runway. The most significant dissent came from Buffett and Greenblatt, who argued that at 56x EV/FCF the stock prices in years of future earnings with insufficient margin of safety, and that no business quality, however exceptional, excuses paying a premium multiple without a bargain price. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged that traditional valuation frameworks underweight the pace and magnitude of AI-driven revenue compounding, a structural shift the dissenters' models are not designed to capture. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels with disciplined sizing reflecting the elevated multiple.

rows.name: Amgen Inc.
rows.statement: The Committee assigns Amgen Inc. a BUY rating with a composite score of 0.632. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and Joel Greenblatt and carrying the majority, holds that at approximately 16× forward earnings, the market is modestly under-pricing a business generating $10 billion in annual free cash flow on 48% non-GAAP operating margins with genuinely high returns on tangible capital — an attractive earnings yield on a durable franchise whose quality is not fully reflected in the current price. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett, who argued that the enterprise value of $243 billion, burdened by substantial acquisition-related debt from the Horizon transaction, does not offer a sufficient margin of safety relative to the business's intrinsic worth. This concern, while disciplined and well-reasoned, did not prevail because the majority judged the valuation discount and cash-flow durability sufficient to compensate for the elevated leverage. Cathie Wood's disruption-oriented objection was noted but deemed outside the Committee's primary valuation framework. The Committee recommends initiating a position at current levels.

rows.name: NVIDIA Corp.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) a final score of 0.556 and adopts a **BUY** position. The dominant argument carrying the majority, advanced most forcefully by Leopold Aschenbrenner and Cathie Wood, holds that NVIDIA occupies the central infrastructure node of a discontinuous AI compute buildout, and that at 18x forward earnings with 106% year-over-year revenue growth, 75% gross margins, and $215.9 billion in annual revenue, the stock is not stretched by any growth-adjusted measure. The most significant dissent, articulated by Warren Buffett, Howard Marks, and Joel Greenblatt, centered on the inability to project NVIDIA's competitive position over a ten-year horizon given advancing custom silicon from hyperscalers, and on the risk embedded in a $5.37 trillion market capitalization where consensus enthusiasm leaves little margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because the near-term earnings trajectory and forward multiple were judged insufficiently demanding to justify a pass. The Committee recommends a measured BUY with position sizing reflecting the elevated valuation and competitive uncertainty noted by the minority.

rows.name: American Express Co.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns American Express a BUY rating with a conviction score of 0.333, reflecting a narrow majority. The dominant argument, advanced principally by Mr. Buffett, holds that American Express's closed-loop, three-party network constitutes a durable and difficult-to-replicate competitive moat, generating proprietary spending data and genuine switching costs on both sides of the platform — qualities that justify ownership at a sensible, if not discounted, price. The most significant dissent, articulated by Messrs. Marks and Greenblatt, contended that the business's acknowledged quality is already reflected in a valuation of roughly 20x trailing earnings, offering insufficient margin of safety absent a catalyst or mispricing event. This dissent did not prevail because the majority judged the franchise's compounding power and network durability to be inadequately captured by static valuation metrics alone. The Committee recommends initiating a modest position in AXP, with sizing calibrated to the low conviction score and a mandate to reassess should valuation expand further without commensurate earnings acceleration.

rows.name: Honeywell International Inc.
rows.statement: After full deliberation, the Committee assigns Honeywell Technologies (HON) a final position of **BUY** with a conviction score of **0.312**, reflecting a narrow but affirmative majority. The dominant argument, advanced principally by Howard Marks, held that the post-aerospace spinoff has created a pure-play automation company whose transformation premium is not yet fully captured by the market; the trailing P/E of 9.4x, while distorted by the mid-transformation earnings base, signals that consensus has yet to converge on the business's intrinsic value, and the 140-year installed base provides meaningful downside protection through genuine switching costs. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that the forward P/E of 26.6x represents the honest price tag and that the market has already priced in the restructuring upside, leaving insufficient margin of safety. This dissent did not prevail because it underweighted the second-level opportunity embedded in spinoff-driven mispricing and mid-cycle industrial positioning. The Committee recommends initiating a modest position with disciplined sizing commensurate with the low conviction score.

rows.name: UnitedHealth Group Inc.
rows.statement: After thorough deliberation, the Committee assigns UnitedHealth Group a final score of **0.312** and a position of **BUY**. The dominant argument, advanced by Howard Marks and carrying the majority, held that the stock's meaningful pullback — trading at roughly 22× forward earnings following an earnings beat of $6.38 versus $4.90 expected — has priced in substantial headwinds, creating a favorable risk-reward asymmetry for a business of this scale and competitive position. The most significant dissent came from Warren Buffett and Joel Greenblatt, who argued that UnitedHealth's moat is narrower than it appears — insurance offers standardized policies with limited pricing power, Optum's returns on capital are difficult to isolate with confidence, and regulatory and reputational risks remain genuine and unquantifiable. This dissent did not prevail because the Committee judged these risks to be largely reflected in the current valuation rather than incremental to it. The Committee recommends a **modest buy**, sized conservatively to reflect the low-conviction nature of the majority position and the substantive quality of the dissent.
